title: Agent Memory Is Solved. Agent Learning Isn't. — Karthik Ranganathan, Yugabyte
talk_summary: Karthik argues that per-agent memory is largely solved, but multi-agent learning fails because agents share outputs without reasoning, dead ends, and provenance, forcing repeated token-burning rederivation. He demos a Mako data-pack/MCP layer where agents write private context, promote selected facts to shared spaces, resume sessions across agents, and trace decisions/tool calls.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents write context into a private data pack, then explicitly promote selected high-quality facts into a shared space that other agents and humans can retrieve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents to come in and push pieces of their context into a private space and promote that to a shared space
be able to trace it back to something, a data source, a person, a conversation from which it was extracted

takeaways.what_they_do: Use an MCP memory server so a new session or different agent can retrieve prior conversation/facts by tool call instead of relying on IDE project memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The difference here is just an MCP tool call.

takeaways.what_they_do: The first agent records a failing external dependency or command in shared memory; other agents check it before retrying.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the first agent would hit it and then tell everybody that it happened and all the other agents would know that it already happened

takeaways.technique: Tune retrieval with traces, fewer chunks
takeaways.what_they_do: Trace retrieval, change one variable at a time, and shrink context to higher-precision chunks rather than dumping more memory or RAG transcripts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Our context chunks, which is the context size, went down from over 7,000 chunks to about a,000 chunks
takeaways.numbers: faithfulness 14% MD / 20% PDF and 57% context precision improved to 65/74/82; chunks >7,000 -> ~1,000

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat human approve/reject decisions on shared memories as labeled examples for future retrieval and promotion policies.
takeaways.evidence_quote: human promotions today kind of equal the training signal for self-improving orchestration tomorrow
